title: Green chemistry
examples: What is the difference between green chemistry and sustainable chemistry?
Can you give an example of a reaction that has poor atom economy?
How does designing reactions matter for the environment?

explain.say: Green chemistry is about designing chemical products and processes.
The first principle suggests we should prevent waste rather than treating it later.
Another key idea is using safer chemical substances in the first place.
Atom economy measures how much starting material ends up in the desired product.

draw.text: Atom Economy: Desired Mass / Total Mass

explain.say: Consider the reaction making ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen gas.
In this reaction, all atoms from the starting materials are in the product.

faq.q: What is the difference between green chemistry and sustainable chemistry?
faq.a: Green chemistry is a set of guidelines for designing chemical processes to reduce pollution. Sustainability is a broader concept that includes environmental, social, and economic aspects.
asks: How does green chemistry relate to the environment?

faq.q: Does atom economy only apply to addition reactions?
faq.a: No, atom economy applies to any chemical reaction. It helps us calculate the efficiency of any synthesis method.
asks: Must I use atom economy for all reactions?

faq.q: Can you name a reaction with very low atom economy?
faq.a: Reactions involving the formation of large amounts of salt byproducts often have low atom economy. These byproducts are waste.
asks: What is a bad example of atom economy?
How much waste can I expect?

faq.q: Why is preventing waste better than treating it?
faq.a: Preventing waste is better because it saves energy and resources needed for disposal methods. Treating waste still requires energy and often creates secondary pollution.
asks: Is waste treatment always energy intensive?
What is the cost of waste disposal?

faq.q: What are the 12 principles in detail?
faq.a: The twelve principles cover everything from using safer materials to designing for energy efficiency. They provide a framework for chemists to improve processes.
asks: Are there many principles to remember?
Can I list all twelve principles?

facts: Green chemistry aims to minimize or eliminate the use and generation of hazardous substances.
Atom economy is calculated by dividing the molecular mass of the desired product by the sum of the molecular masses of all reactants.
A reaction with 100 percent atom economy means all starting atoms end up in the final product.
Safer solvents, like water, are preferred over volatile organic compounds.

quiz.say: In a reaction where A + B → C + D, if C is the desired product, what does a low atom economy suggest?

options.show: The reaction produces a lot of unwanted byproducts.
options.say: The reaction produces a lot of unwanted byproducts.

quiz.why: A low atom economy means many atoms from the starting materials end up as waste instead of the main product.

wrong.0: Rate of reaction is about speed, not the amount of waste.
wrong.1: Cost is an economic factor, not a chemical efficiency measure.
wrong.2: Instability relates to the product's structure, not the overall mass balance.

quiz.say: Which principle focuses on designing reactions to use less energy?
quiz.why: This principle encourages using ambient temperature and pressure conditions to save energy.

wrong.0: Reactant state is not the main focus of energy efficiency.
wrong.1: This increases energy use, which the principle seeks to avoid.
wrong.2: Catalysts help, but the principle focuses on minimizing external energy input.

quiz.say: If the reaction is 2CH4 + O2 → 2CO2 + 2H2O, what is the atom economy?

options.show: It is based only on the mass of CO2.
options.say: It is based only on the mass of CO2.

options.show: It is zero because water is a byproduct.
options.say: It is zero because water is a byproduct.

options.show: The calculation must include all atoms in the desired product.
options.say: The calculation must include all atoms in the desired product.

options.show: It is 100% because all atoms are used.
options.say: It is 100% because all atoms are used.

quiz.why: The calculation must compare the mass of the desired product (CO2 + H2O) to the total mass of reactants (2CH4 + O2).

wrong.0: The atom economy must account for all desired products listed.
wrong.1: Water is part of the desired output, not just waste.
wrong.3: While all atoms are used, the calculation requires specific mass ratios.
